_meta.description: Second, parallel eval set alongside eval/eval-set.json (Airbnb domain, do not modify). Covers the Shelfline e-commerce domain: a white-label storefront + seller-console SaaS brief (Google Drive doc product-brief-shelfline.md), written explicitly to generate a realistic spread of UI component needs for testing Pattern's recommend_component judgment.
_meta.domain: Shelfline -- white-label e-commerce storefront + seller dashboard SaaS for independent brands (apparel, home goods, specialty food), starter tier (<500 SKUs)
_meta.verification_note: Two tiers of gold quality, distinguished per-item by the 'verified' field. verified:true items were independently confirmed by fetching the actual cited candidate's real docs page (WebFetch, not through Pattern) and hand-checking the requirement against real content -- see 'verification_source'. verified:false or absent means the gold value is a prediction (either this brief's own stated expectation, or an observation from a live run) that has NOT been independently confirmed against a real component's actual capabilities -- treat these the same as eval-set.json's original unverified gold answers, not as ground truth.
_meta.known_findings: The brief predicted checkout, stepper, and uploader would need custom builds. All three independently verified as genuine use_existing matches against a real library (ReUI, reui.io) -- the brief's prediction was wrong, not Pattern's verdict. But the same independent check caught two real evidence errors inside Pattern's own requirements_checked for these cases: an invented 'nonInteractive' stepper mode that isn't real (the real docs only show a more limited 'disabled' prop), and a missed real 'maxFiles' cap parameter on the uploader that Pattern incorrectly marked as unsupported. These two are the seed regression cases for testing whether fetch-grounded scoring (see the project plan) fixes them.

cases.component_need: Multi-step checkout (shipping info -> payment -> review) for a simple single-address, single-payment-method flow -- no split payments, no multi-currency, no saved-address book beyond what Stripe Elements already handles

gold.rationale: Brief predicted custom_build. Independently confirmed via reui.io/blocks/ecommerce/checkout: real 4-step flow (contact/delivery/payment/review), sticky order summary with tax/discount lines, and card/PayPal/Apple Pay switching all real. No Stripe Elements wiring included, matching Pattern's own NOT MET call on that item.

requirements.requirement: Step indicator/progress UI showing shipping -> payment -> review stages
Shipping address form with validation
Payment step integrated with Stripe Elements (PaymentElement or similar)
Review step showing order summary, address, payment method, totals
Navigation between steps (next/back) with state persistence
Form validation and error handling per step
Order total calculation display (subtotal, shipping, tax, total)
Final submit/place order action that creates a payment intent / confirms order

cases.component_need: Fulfillment-status stepper (pending -> packed -> shipped -> delivered) for an order detail view

gold.rationale: Brief predicted custom_build. Independently confirmed via reui.io/docs/stepper: real Stepper built on Base UI/Radix with StepperItem/StepperIndicator/StepperSeparator/StepperTitle/StepperDescription sub-components, horizontal+vertical orientation, active/completed/inactive/loading states -- all real. KNOWN ERROR: Pattern's own run claimed a 'nonInteractive' read-only mode 'intended for status/order-tracking displays' -- the real docs describe no such mode, only a more limited 'disabled' prop on StepperItem. This is an invented feature, the seed regression case for the fetch-grounded-scoring fix.

requirements.requirement: Displays a sequence of discrete fulfillment stages (pending, packed, shipped, delivered) as ordered steps
Distinct visual indicator per state (pending/upcoming, current/active, completed)
Checkmark or icon confirmation for completed steps
Connector line between steps reflecting progress
Per-step label with associated date/timestamp (e.g. 'Shipped Aug 12')
Responsive layout switching between horizontal and vertical orientation
Support for exception/edge states (cancelled, delayed, returned) beyond the happy path
Accessible semantic markup and state handling for screen readers

gold.known_error_note: Pattern's clean-baseline component_description claimed a 'nonInteractive' read-only status-tracking mode. Verified false -- not documented anywhere on reui.io/docs/stepper. This is an evidence fabrication, not a requirements_checked item per se (it appeared in component_description prose), but is the primary regression signal for this case: rerun after the fetch-grounded-scoring fix and confirm this claim no longer appears.

cases.component_need: Drag-to-reorder image uploader for a product's photo set, capped at 8 images

gold.rationale: Brief predicted custom_build. Independently confirmed via reui.io/docs/file-upload: real File Upload component with a 'Sortable Upload' variant, click+drag-and-drop, per-image remove and progress. KNOWN ERROR: Pattern's own run marked 'hard cap enforcement' NOT MET, claiming 'no mention of a configurable max-count prop' -- the real docs document a maxFiles parameter (type: number, default: Infinity) directly contradicting that. This is the second seed regression case. The Sortable Upload sub-component's specific drag mechanics (keyboard accessibility, exact reorder behavior) could not be independently confirmed -- that page renders client-side and WebFetch only sees static HTML; treat those specific items as unverified, not confirmed either way.

requirements.requirement: Drag-and-drop reordering of image thumbnails in a grid
requirements.verification_note: Sortable Upload variant exists and is named for this purpose, but its specific page renders client-side -- WebFetch could not confirm the reorder mechanics directly.

requirements.requirement: Multi-file upload via click-to-browse and OS drag-and-drop
Hard cap enforcement (exactly 8 images, disables further uploads past limit)
requirements.verification_note: KNOWN ERROR CASE: Pattern's clean-baseline run marked this NOT MET. Real docs document a maxFiles parameter (type: number, default: Infinity) that satisfies this -- Pattern missed a real capability.

requirements.requirement: Per-image remove/delete control
Per-image upload progress indicator
Primary/cover image designation (e.g., first photo flagged as main product image)
Consistent-aspect-ratio thumbnail grid layout for product photos
Keyboard-accessible drag-and-drop reordering (a11y)

cases.component_need: Hero banner with a full-bleed background image, centered headline/subhead, and a single CTA button, for a brand's homepage

gold.rationale: Brief's own 'likely clean match' category. Live run (2026-08-28) returned use_existing at 4/8 (50%), low confidence -- lower than the brief's own expectation for a case it called a clean match. Not independently re-verified against a real candidate's docs this pass; flagged as worth a closer look given the gap between predicted and observed confidence.

cases.component_need: Toast notification system for confirming actions (item added to cart, product saved, order updated) across both storefront and console

gold.rationale: Brief's own 'likely clean match' category, and the live run (2026-08-28) matched that expectation exactly: 100% coverage, high confidence, no ensemble trigger. Not independently re-verified against a real candidate's docs this pass.

cases.component_need: Empty-state pattern (icon, short message, single CTA) for a category with no products, an order list with no orders, and a review section with no reviews yet

gold.rationale: Brief's own 'likely clean match' category, matched by the live run (2026-08-28): 100% coverage, high confidence, no ensemble trigger. Not independently re-verified against a real candidate's docs this pass.

cases.component_need: Tabbed settings layout (Store details, Shipping, Payments, Notifications) for the seller console settings page

gold.rationale: Brief's own 'likely clean match' category, roughly matched by the live run (2026-08-28): high confidence, 85.7% coverage, though the ensemble did trigger (close to the 80% threshold). Not independently re-verified against a real candidate's docs this pass.

cases.component_need: Category page filter sidebar with checkbox groups for size, color, and price range, collapsible on mobile into a slide-over panel

gold.rationale: Brief flagged this category specifically to watch for Pattern recommending something heavier than a starter-tier need requires (the same proportionality-mismatch failure pattern documented for the original Airbnb eval set's date-range-picker/availability-calendar cases). Live run (2026-08-28) returned 100% coverage, high confidence -- but whether the cited candidate is actually right-sized (not an enterprise data-grid style component) was NOT independently checked this pass. This is the highest-priority case to verify next given the brief's explicit warning.

cases.component_need: Product list table with inline status toggle (active/draft), thumbnail, name, price, and inventory count, for a catalog of roughly 50-500 products, with basic column sort but no need for column reordering, grouping, or pivoting

gold.rationale: Same proportionality-risk category as filter-sidebar above -- the brief explicitly calls out product/order tables as the case most likely to produce a scope mismatch (recommending column reordering/grouping/pivoting machinery a 50-500 row starter-tier catalog doesn't need). Live run (2026-08-28) returned 100% coverage, high confidence. NOT independently checked against the real cited candidate's actual feature surface this pass -- high priority for the next verification round.

cases.component_need: Order list table with filter by status and date range, and search by order number or customer name, for order volumes in the low thousands per month at this tier

gold.rationale: Same proportionality-risk category as filter-sidebar and product-table above. Live run (2026-08-28) returned 100% coverage, high confidence. NOT independently checked against the real cited candidate's actual feature surface this pass.

Brief's vague-vs-specific contrast pair against product-table and order-table above. Live run (2026-08-28) returned 71.4% coverage, low confidence -- meaningfully lower than either specific counterpart's 100%, consistent with the README's warning that vague category names produce weaker/more misleading matches, though not low enough to flip the verdict to custom_build in this case. Not independently re-verified against a real candidate's docs this pass.
